claim_kind: complexity lower bound (no polynomial kernel unless coNP ⊆ NP/poly; WK[1]-hardness)
reason: Core claim is about polynomial-time reductions and kernels. Without a computation model it is trivial (map to a fixed instance), and the noncrossing plane-routing model needs embeddings that Mathlib does not provide.

claim_kind: conditional existence of a space-bounded randomized online learner with high-probability regret bound
reason: No faithful formal model is available for word-RAM space with real-valued scalars and counted workspace in online randomized learners. The hypothesis is an elaborate probabilistic interface (random partitions, sigma-fields, conditional independence, certificates on a good event) over a family of online components. Every simplification either makes the S-word space bound vacuous or changes the theorem.

claim_kind: kernel lower bound / WK[1]-hardness via polynomial-parameter transformation
reason: Core claim is a conditional kernel lower bound / WK[1]-hardness; the reduction's existence is trivial without running time, the gadget construction is unspecified, and non-crossing plane routing needs embeddings absent from Mathlib.

claim_kind: complexity_class_inclusion
reason: Core claim is an inclusion of uniform, space/time-bounded quantum state-synthesis complexity classes (with an interactive quantum verifier and an assumed PSPACE solver); no quantum circuit, interactive-proof, or space-bounded computation model exists in Mathlib or TCSlib, so the statement cannot be expressed faithfully without inventing the entire computational model, and dropping the resource bounds makes it trivially true (unbounded circuits prepare any state exactly).

claim_kind: algorithm existence + running time
reason: Core claim is a running-time bound for a sampling algorithm; Mathlib/TCSlib have no randomized RAM cost model, and dropping the time bound leaves a trivial statement.

claim_kind: deterministic fully dynamic algorithm with worst-case update time n^{3/2+o(1)}
reason: Core claim is a worst-case update-time bound for a dynamic data structure assembled from hypothesized offline algorithms with time bounds; dropping time leaves nothing faithful.

claim_kind: existence of an explicit generator with uniform logspace reconstruction
reason: If uniformity of G_n and the space bound on R are dropped, the statement becomes trivial: a random map with seed length O(log n) fools every size-n^2 predictor (probabilistic method), so the implication is vacuous. Stating it faithfully needs a circuit model, a space-bounded transducer model, and an explicit NW/direct-product construction built from four black-box primitives with space bounds, none of which exist at this pin.

claim_kind: existence of uniform hitting-set generator H, probabilistic oracle reconstruction algorithm R, and succinct-description transformation A_H with resource bounds
reason: The core claim is a statement about the running time of R and the uniformity, description length, space and depth of the generator. Without these bounds it is trivial: R can compute C_U(1^n) directly. Stating it faithfully needs space-bounded succinct circuit descriptions, oracle circuits and time-bounded probabilistic oracle machines, and none of these exist in TCSlib or Mathlib.

claim_kind: asymptotic indistinguishability bound over all q-query algorithms
reason: The breaking oracle W^R takes as addresses classical descriptions of quantum circuits C that it executes on postselected transcript states |psi_v^P>, with domain-separated random-oracle tags, layer registers and joint distributions over (O,O',z,H). A faithful statement needs a model of quantum circuits as data plus an interpreter, conditioned post-measurement states, quantification over all q-query algorithms with external randomness, and an unspecified poly(q) factor; no TCSlib/Mathlib infrastructure exists and any ad hoc encoding (e.g. fixing the circuit semantics or the poly) would change the claim.

claim_kind: algorithm existence with parallel oracle complexity bounds (query depth, total queries, computational depth, scalar work)
reason: Core claim is a parallel stochastic-oracle complexity bound (query depth/work) for an implementation of an assumed abstract procedure; no oracle-algorithm/query-depth model exists in Mathlib or TCSlib, and dropping the cost bounds makes the remaining accuracy claim trivial.

claim_kind: oracle separation / impossibility of fully black-box construction (IV-PoQ from iO + OWP)
reason: Requires a model of QPT/PPT interactive oracle algorithms, coherent quantum queries to stateful oracles, idealized iO and OWP security against polynomial-query quantum adversaries, and fully black-box reductions; none exist in Mathlib/TCSlib, and removing efficiency makes the statement vacuous (unbounded classical provers simulate quantum ones).

claim_kind: black-box separation / impossibility of reductions
reason: The core claim is a meta-theorem about quantum polynomial-time black-box reductions, falsifiable assumptions secure against non-uniform QPT adversaries with quantum advice, and 'infinitely many λ' inverse-polynomial advantages. It requires a computational model of uniform/non-uniform quantum polynomial time and interactive protocols, none of which exist in Mathlib/TCSlib; the only purely mathematical residues (choosing the best first message, n = ⌈128 q² p²⌉ arithmetic) are trivial and would not capture the theorem.

claim_kind: RE-completeness of a promise problem under polynomial-time reductions via efficient Kleene recursion theorem
reason: The core argument hinges on running-time hypotheses (TIME_{S_e}(n) <= n^a, compressed sequence time p_a(|e|)(1+log n)^gamma) and an efficient fixed-point theorem with polynomial index/time overhead. Mathlib/TCSlib have no time-bounded programming system: Code.evaln fuel is a step-index not polynomially related to TM time (simulating a machine via a primrec evaln code needs fuel far beyond poly), so the fixed-point sequence could not provably meet the n^a hypothesis and the statement would be unprovable for modelling reasons. Dropping the time clause instead strengthens the compression hypothesis to all total sequences with a computable threshold, which may be inconsistent and would trivialize/alter the claim. Abstracting time and the recursion theorem as axioms would require inventing a whole programming-system framework whose closure axioms essentially encode the proof.

claim_kind: oracle-complexity upper bound (existence of randomized first-order sampler with high-probability query bound)
reason: Core claim is an oracle query-complexity bound for a randomized continuous-space sampling algorithm using black-box primitives that are themselves complexity statements; no oracle-algorithm model over R^d exists and removing the query count trivializes the claim.

claim_kind: oracle-complexity upper bound (first-order + proximal oracle sampler under LSI)
reason: Core claim is an oracle query-complexity bound with black-box algorithmic hypotheses; no model of randomized oracle algorithms over R^d in Mathlib/TCSlib, and dropping complexity trivializes the statement.

claim_kind: oracle-complexity upper bound (proximal sampler for weakly log-concave targets, KL accuracy)
